To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a solution of the Maxwell system describing time-dependent electromagnetic wave propagation in one-dimensional inhomogeneous media is obtained in terms of Darboux transmutation operators and Fourier-Legendre series of their integral kernels.

the time-dependent Maxwell system in inhomogeneous media reduces to a Vukua-type equation for functions of a hyperbolically extended time variable, that the solution of this equation in the general case can be obtained by means of Darboux transmutation operators, that the Fourier-Legendre series expansion of the integral kernels of transmutations can be used to represent the transmitted signal in terms of a series of Bessel function, and that the representation can be used for numerical computation of the signal.
we obtained exact solution for the transmission of electromagnetic wave through an inhomogeneous layer in terms of transmutations and Neumann series of the Bessel functions.

the study of the time-dependent one-dimensional Maxwell system describing electromagnetic (EM) wave propagation in in homogeneous isotropic media.
a generalization of the classical theory of diffraction to the case of electromagnetic waves propagating in time-dependent inhomogeneous media.
a new exact solution of the one-dimensional time-dependent Maxwell system.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in the present paper a general solution of Maxwell system in the one-dimensional time-dependent case in inhomogeneous media is given in terms of transmutation and Neumann series of special functions, which is a significant step in the direction of solving a problem of great importance in applications.

the exact representation of the solution of the transmission problem in terms of transmutation operators and Neumann series of special functions is a new and efficient tool in the analysis and computation of time-dependent electromagnetic wave propagation in one-dimensional inhomogeneous media.
in the one-dimensional time-dependent case we were able to obtain an exact representation of the solution in terms of transmutations and Fourier-Legendre series.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the exact solution of the time-dependent Maxwell system in the one-dimensional inhomogeneous media can be obtained in the form of a Neumann series of special functions.

the solution of the transmission problem for a modulated electromagnetic wave in an arbitrary inhomogenous layer can be written as an explicit Neumann series with exact formulas for coefficients in terms of the Fourier-Legendre series of the transmutation kernel.

in the classical case of a trigonometrical Fourier series the problem of the electromagnetic wave transmission through an inhomogeneous layer can be efficiently solved by using a Neumann series of bessel functions.
